topic: The Ternary Code of Sierpinski: From Towers of Hanoi to Fractals
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Logic of Base-3
lecture_lines: Base-3 uses digits zero, one, and two.
Robot movement maps to ternary sequences.
animations: Create three labeled points (A, B, C) in #FFFFFF.
Animate a path segment connecting A to B in #FFFF00.
Show label '0' near the A to B path.
Show label '1' near the B to C path.
Show label '2' near the A to C path in #FF0000.

sections.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Constrained Hanoi limits moves to adjacent pegs.
Moves A to B are zero.
Moves B to C are one.
Illegal moves are represented by two.
Legal paths exclude the digit two.
animations: Draw three pegs labeled A, B, C in #FFFFFF.
Represent disk moves as a colored line between pegs.

sections.title: Visualizing the Sierpinski Triangle
lecture_lines: State space forms the Sierpinski Triangle.
Each turn adds a ternary digit.
animations: Draw a large Sierpinski triangle in #FFFFFF.
Display an ant moving along edges.
Highlight triangle vertices with ternary digits (0, 1, 2).

sections.title: Synthesis: The Fractal Geometry of Computation
lecture_lines: Hanoi moves map to Sierpinski points.
Infinite recursion creates the geometric limit.
animations: Morph state diagram into triangle shape.
